 Order
The offence involved in this case is under Sections 420 & 498A of the Indian Penal Code, 1808.

The second respondent, who is the de facto complainant, has filed an affidavit dated 12.09.2024 stating that she had re-married and she is permanently settled in the United Kingdom, and hence not interested in proceeding with this criminal prosecution against the petitioners.
The counsel representing the second respondent also submitted that the matter has been amicably settled between the parties.

2. In the light of the above statement in the affidavit filed by the de facto complainant as well as the submissions of the learned counsel for the de facto complainant about the settlement of the issue,
there is no need to proceed further with this criminal prosecution as against the petitioners since it would be an abuse of process of court.

It has been held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in B.S. Joshy v.
State of Haryana [(2003) 4 SCC 675] that in matrimonial issues, it would not be proper to decline to exercise power of quashing the proceedings under Section 482 Cr.P.C when the parties have sorted out their issues.
